conviction_note: The findings roughly cancel (impact_sum -0.1). Small positive peer and storage-demand reads offset a positioning negative: the stock is +13% in 20 days, +9.5% in 5, 4% off its 52-week high, and six price-target raises since 5 Oct have taken it above the average target. That is the same set-up as July, when a clean beat with a flat sequential subscription guide sold off -19.7%. The scaled number is (2*0.47-1)*14 = -0.84. p_up sits only 3 points under 50 because the call-side skew and an open sale process both argue against a short.
bar: Company guide for Q2 FY27: subscription revenue $264-268M, non-GAAP EBIT margin ~20% (Q1 FY27 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001169561/000116956126000020/q1fy27pressrelease.htm). Sell-side consensus: total revenue $310.8M, EPS $1.25, unrevised over 30 days (Zacks via Yahoo, 2026-10-22, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/unlocking-q2-potential-commvault-cvlt-121507687.html). A second aggregator agrees at $310.28M / $1.24 (https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/10/25/commvault-systems-cvlt-expected-to-post-earnings-on-tuesday.html). Zacks's subscription line ($263.16M) uses a different definition from the restated company line, so I size against the company guide. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against the $266M subscription midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 7.7% of float with 4.3 days to cover (Equibles, as of 2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/cvlt/summary). Another source shows 3.21M shares and 5.59 days at the 2026-08-14 settlement (https://altindex.com/ticker/cvlt/short-interest). I found no October settlement. That is moderate, not crowded. Skew_25d is -6.05 vol points, meaning calls are bid ('upside paid'), but the chain is thin: 270 total open interest and an ATM spread of 19% of mid. Part of the call bid is probably takeover optionality, since a sale process has been reported as open since April, rather than a view on the print. Run-up is +13.0% over 20 days and +9.5% over 5. Analyst targets were raised into the print: Scotiabank $160 (10-05), RBC $160 (10-08), Mizuho $185 (10-12/15), Baird $180 (10-19), Cantor $171 (10-26), Jefferies $170 Hold (10-26). Spot of $167.36 is above the MarketBeat/StockAnalysis average target of $160.7-163.5.

findings.finding: Q2 subscription revenue is guided to $264-268M, flat to down from Q1's actual $267.0M, and Q1 term-license revenue grew only +1% while management cited a term-duration headwind as customers assessed hardware/storage plans. On its own record Commvault guides conservatively: Q1 beat EPS $1.42 vs $1.16 and revenue $314.1M vs $310.5M. A beat of the $266M midpoint by ~1-2% is therefore the base case, but that is a quarter the company told the market to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold. Q1 FY27 (2026-07-28): EPS beat by $0.26 and revenue beat, stock -19.7% on the flat sequential subscription guide. 2026-01-27: -31.1%. 2025-10-28: -16.3%. Only 2026-04-28 (+10.8%) paid for a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Consensus already sits at the guide ($310.8M total revenue), and a beat of a conservative guide is the expected outcome. Had the market priced a large upside surprise, Zacks's EPS estimate would have been revised up in the last 30 days; it was not.
findings.independence: The term-duration/hardware comment comes from a secondary summary of the 2026-07-28 call, which shares the event with this release (https://www.tickerreport.com/?p=13519146, 404 at fetch; quoted in search snippet). The July sell-off rationale is in https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/28/why-commvault-stock-crashed-today/

findings.finding: Rubrik, the closest listed cyber-resilience/backup peer, reported its July quarter on 2026-08-27, after Commvault last spoke. It exceeded every guided metric, raised every FY27 metric, and grew subscription ARR to $1.66B with net new subscription ARR +35% YoY and Cloud ARR +39%. That points to healthy category demand through Commvault's September quarter, especially for SaaS ARR (Commvault Q1 SaaS ARR $424M, +38%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history of CVLT reacting to Rubrik prints is in the baseline. CVLT's ARR/guide line drove the -19.7% in July and the +10.8% in April.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The 20-day run-up and the October target raises probably already carry some sector read-through. Had it been fully priced, Commvault's FY27 subscription ARR consensus would sit above the $1,200-1,210M guide, and I found no source showing that. Rubrik also takes share partly from Commvault, so the read is a category proxy, not a company number.
findings.independence: Proxy. Rubrik's own release corroborates it: https://www.rubrik.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/26/rubrik-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results (403 at fetch, figures via https://pulse2.com/rubrik-cloud-arr-jumps-39-to-1-48-billion-as-subscription-arr-contribution-margin-expands-460-basis-points/)

findings.finding: NetApp's July quarter (reported late Aug/early Sep 2026) showed revenue +30%, all-flash +47%, a raised FY27 guide and customers accelerating purchases as component costs rose. That is relevant to the on-prem/term-license line Commvault said was soft because customers were 'assessing hardware and storage plans'. A completed storage refresh would tend to unlock the attached backup term license in the September quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 term-license revenue +1% YoY was part of the guide disappointment that preceded the -19.7% move. There is no earlier history of CVLT reacting to the storage cycle in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The macro-to-company transmission has not been confirmed by Commvault, and pulled-forward hardware buying can also delay software decisions. If priced, the sell-side would have lifted Commvault's term-license estimates; Zacks shows no EPS revision in 30 days.
findings.independence: Proxy, and it shares the storage-cycle theme with nothing else here. Dell's record storage revenue (+26%) points the same way: https://www.cnhinews.com/news/article_5d680f27-4b3d-50ba-bdc5-90a4de5f6a40.html

findings.finding: Into the print the stock is +9.5% over 5 sessions and +13.0% over 20, within 4% of its 52-week high and above the average analyst target ($160.7-163.5). Six target raises landed between 5 and 26 Oct, three of them from Neutral/Hold houses chasing the price (Cantor $132→$171, Jefferies $130→$170, Scotiabank $130→$160). This repeats the July set-up: Truist raised to $182 a week before, then a beat with a flat guide sold off -19.7%. A print that only meets the bar has room to fall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a 92% rally into July, a beat with a soft guide gave -19.7%. Of the last four prints, three fell by 16-31%.
findings.why_not_priced: The option market leans the other way: skew -6.05, with calls bid. So the market is paying for upside, not hedging a give-back. The reason I think the option market is wrong about this print is that the chain is thin (270 OI, ATM spread 19% of mid) and its call bid more plausibly prices takeover optionality than the quarter. Short interest of ~7.7% / 4-6 days is not crowded enough to make a squeeze the dominant mechanism.
findings.independence: Jefferies Hold at $170, 2026-10-26: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9142359/cvlt-maintained-by-jefferies-price-target-raised-to-170 . Baird/RBC/Mizuho raises: https://www.cnn.com/markets/stocks/CVLT . Run-up from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Reuters reported on 2026-04-10 that Commvault is exploring a sale with Goldman Sachs after takeover interest, including an earlier offer from Thoma Bravo. No company statement or 8-K has closed the process since: EDGAR shows only an 8-K adding director David Morton, the CFO of Intapp, on 2026-09-22, with no mention of it, and an August report says no decision has been made. Companies often disclose a deal or an end to the review alongside results, so the print carries a two-sided tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose ~13-17% on the day of the Reuters report (2026-04-10, to $88.52). There is no history of a print carrying deal news.
findings.why_not_priced: The probability that anything is said on 27 Oct is unknowable from public documents. Some deal premium is already in a stock that has roughly doubled since April. If the market expected an announcement with the print, the event-implied move (12.2%) would sit well above the name's 16.3% median reaction rather than below it.
findings.independence: The August status update (no final decision; may remain independent): https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/software/nasdaq-cvlt/commvault-systems/news/commvault-sale-talks-put-mixed-shareholder-returns-in-fresh . The director 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1169561/000116956126000030/cvlt-20260922.htm

findings.finding: Insiders sold 29,348 shares (~$4.2M) in the three months after the July print, under 10b5-1 plans and largely for tax withholding (CEO 12,437 shares at $143.98 on 08-17). EDGAR shows a cluster of Form 144s on 08-10 and 08-17/20 and no open-market buys.
findings.why_not_priced: Routine and public. It is filed because it is a sourced fact, and sized near zero because these are scheduled tax-withholding sales.

rejected_candidates.detail: Not contradicted. I did not file it because it is a routine patch advisory with no reported exploitation or customer impact on this print; listed here so the panel can disagree. None of the four drop reasons strictly applies.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Zacks subscription-revenue consensus of $263.16M, below the low end of the $264M guide, which would make a beat look larger
rejected_candidates.detail: Its +52.4% YoY tag shows it is on a different definition from the restated subscription line in the 2026-07-28 release (which now includes term-based support), so it is not comparable to the company guide.

baseline_tension: The findings cut against the skew: calls are bid while my only sizeable finding is a positioning negative. They are in line with the run-up as a give-back risk. The reaction history (three of the last four prints fell 16-31%) supports the negative, while the open sale process supports the call bid.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sells its beats): the reported-quarter beat finding goes from +0.5 to +0.3.

Rule 7 (a sign against the skew): the positioning negative goes from -3.0 to -2.5, with an explicit reason the call skew is not a print view (thin chain, takeover optionality). p_up moves from 46 to 47.

Rules 5, 6 and 8 left everything standing: the proxies (Rubrik, NetApp) were already small; the bar is sourced to a company guide plus two agreeing estimates; coverage is broad (~21 analysts), so the thin-coverage rule does not apply.
